tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`: GPT-6.1 Terra Codex model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

Implement a chat-first UI redesign in this isolated worktree. The main session is separately improving reconstruction and refinement reliability. Keep those efforts independent, agree on shared interfaces, and do not duplicate or rewrite its pipelines.

Use planning, independent plan review, bounded implementation and independent implementation review. Reviewers must directly interact with the browser. Make focused commits; do not push or modify the other worktree.

Read AGENTS.md and the current product, source-first, reconstruction and handoff documentation before implementation.

### Product direction

Create a minimal interface using the actual light and dark colour schemes from my Chronicle project. Locate its theme files; if unavailable, ask for their location rather than inventing an approximation.

Initially, show a clean chat interface with blueprint attachments. When visual inspection is requested, move chat to the left and reveal a workspace on the right.

All application operations should be accessible through conversation. Keep manual orbit, zoom and pan. Citations and compact action controls may appear inside chat; avoid separate toolbars, floor selectors and settings panels.

### Target workflow

Support this conversational sequence:

1. Upload blueprint(s).
2. Show “Reading your drawings…” while originals are saved and Gemini creates a validated interpretation.
3. Show that the drawings are ready; source-grounded QA works before 3D.
4. “Show me all windows in the 3D model.”
   - Reuse the current saved model, or invoke the existing reconstruction workflow.
   - Show progress in chat.
   - Open the workspace, highlight reliably associated modeled windows, fade other geometry and frame the selection.
5. “Show this from above.”
   - Move the camera to top-down while preserving selection.
6. “Show the windows individually.”
   - Start a tour that focuses each selected window with a useful close-up orientation.
7. “Show this window in the original blueprint.”
   - Immediately pause the tour and capture the focused object when the message is submitted.
   - Open its original page and highlight its stored evidence region.
8. “Back to the model; next window.”
   - Restore the model and continue the same tour.
9. A requested refinement uses the existing attributed-input, validation and review workflow. Accepted changes update the workspace; rejected changes retain the previous usable model and explain the outcome.

### Architecture

Maintain explicit workspace state: document/revision, view mode, selected IDs, focused ID, camera, tour position, highlighting and assumption visibility.

Use:

Message + captured workspace context → typed action → validation → existing operation → updated chat/workspace

Gemini interprets language; application code resolves and validates identities; deterministic viewer code controls selection, cameras, tours and source navigation. Do not require a VLM to rediscover the focused object from screenshots.

Distinguish navigation commands, factual questions and persistent refinements. Navigation should not unnecessarily invoke the factual QA pipeline. Ask focused clarifications for genuine ambiguity; avoid blanket confirmation steps.

Agree on a small action/result contract before dependent implementation. Own frontend presentation and viewer interaction. Coordinate any backend routing changes with the main session. Do not add a new agent runtime or parallel implementation of reconstruction, QA or persistence.

### Preserve correctness

- Keep Gemini, the provider switch, source-sufficiency gate, citations and refusals.
- Preserve original coordinates, stable IDs, revision-pinned evidence, cached models and portable IFC provenance.
- Generated geometry and display assumptions never become authoritative factual evidence.
- Keep answer highlighting and assumption visibility independently controllable through chat.
- “All modeled windows” must not imply complete extraction of every real window.
- Unresolved objects retain source evidence; never fabricate meshes, matches or tighter source regions.
- Use reliable geometry/host orientation for close-ups; label uncertain orientations appropriately.
- Preserve original labels and building-type agnosticism.
- Keep failed operations and partial models visibly distinguishable from completed, reviewed results.

### Verification and scope

Start with deterministic interaction fixtures to establish layout, navigation and interruption behavior. Clearly distinguish fixtures from real inference. Then verify the workflow against actual saved models and real backend responses.

Independent browser review must exercise both themes, chat/workspace transitions, selections, camera changes, tours, interruption with “this object,” source navigation, assumptions and recoverable failures. Use a real model with renderable windows where available; separately test unresolved objects honestly.

Reuse existing capabilities first. No new formats, models, rendering engines, photorealism or infrastructure. Explain new constraints before introducing them.

Deliver the reviewed implementation, action contract, focused commits and a handoff stating what was verified with fixtures, actual artifacts and live providers, plus remaining gaps.

Entire is enabled for this repo (`gh/Programmercloud-cmd/JunctionHack26`, auto-detected from the git origin remote). Run `entire agent-help` to see what entire does and which subcommand fits, then `entire agent-help <command>` for its exact, current flags. Commits capture the AI session as a checkpoint automatically; only create checkpoints manually when the user asks. If a setup or destructive command (enable, disable, clean, auth) is needed, always ask the user before running it.

I’ll confirm the isolated worktree, read the current contracts and handoff, and locate Chronicle’s theme files. Then I’ll use a planner and independent browser reviewers to agree on a small action contract and keep the UI work separate from reconstruction and refinement.

/goal Implement and integrate the product described below: progressive, source-grounded building reconstruction; JSON-mediated building reasoning; reviewed Q&A; persistent building bundles; and the existing browser-based concept presentation layer.

Work autonomously through planning, independent plan review, bounded implementation, integration, live verification and independent implementation review. Continue beyond planning until the agreed acceptance flows work or a concrete external blocker prevents further progress.

I will be offline. Resolve routine implementation decisions using the repository instructions, existing architecture and your judgment. Communicate assumptions and tradeoffs in progress updates without turning them into approval requests. Preserve existing working behavior and keep the implementation appropriate for this hackathon.

PRODUCT CONCEPT

The product uses two source-grounded review loops: one progressively improves the building model; the other checks answers before publishing them. Both preserve original evidence, explicit uncertainty and traceable revisions.

A saved building can be reopened immediately. New drawings run through background reconstruction; questions reuse the available model and evidence.

Users can switch between:
- Inspection mode: source-associated geometry, evidence, assumptions, unresolved issues and answer highlights.
- Concept mode: an architectural presentation of the same building, with clearly distinguished styling and decorative proposals.

The core experience is:

Upload or open a building, explore its 3D interpretation, and ask questions whose answers link back to the supplied evidence.

All supported inputs expose structured building context for reasoning, while the evidence rules depend on where the information came from.

INPUT PATHS AND JSON-MEDIATED BUILDING REASONING

Implement a structured reasoning interface for genuine IFC files, drawings/PDFs and our drawing-generated IFCs.

JSON makes the information usable for Gemini and deterministic code. It must preserve provenance rather than become an unqualified replacement for the source.

Inspect and reuse existing extraction, description, source-context and artifact functionality before adding new mappings. Do not duplicate capabilities that already exist.

1. Genuine uploaded IFC → reasoning JSON

Use IfcOpenShell to extract a semantic building representation containing:
- Stable IFC GlobalIds, entity types and names.
- Storeys and supported containment relationships.
- Available properties, quantities and units.
- Opening/host and space-boundary relationships where supplied.
- Relevant geometry summaries and deterministic calculations.
- Provenance for each value: supplied property or calculated result.
- Calculation methods and contributing records where relevant.
- Extraction coverage, missing data and unresolved relationships.

Include relevant geometry-less entities in the semantic catalog. Rendering availability must not determine which records can support factual answers.

Preserve references to the original IFC records. Do not invent drawing pages, citation boxes or relationships that the IFC does not provide.

Native IFC facts describe the supplied model, not guaranteed as-built reality.

Do not require Gemini to read raw IFC text or reconstruct an existing IFC. IfcOpenShell performs extraction and supported geometry operations.

2. Drawing/PDF → interpretation JSON plus original evidence

Reuse the building description and source mappings, exposing them through the shared reasoning interface.

Gemini must retain access to original pages and relevant regions. Extracted JSON is a fallible interpretation, not a replacement for the drawing.

Keep observed information, inferred interpretations and display assumptions distinct. Generated dimensions and decorative proposals must not enter factual QA as evidence.

3. Drawing-generated IFC → restored drawing context

When reopening our generated IFC, restore its embedded description, original pages, source mappings and assumptions.

Do not treat generated properties or geometry as authoritative native-IFC evidence merely because the file format is IFC.

Recover the embedded exact description where available instead of unnecessarily reconstructing it from the generated geometry.

4. Shared reasoning interface

Define a common interface for objects, relationships, evidence references, units, provenance and coverage while retaining source-specific detail.

The native-IFC extraction schema and drawing-description schema may remain different.

Do not perform a lossy conversion of arbitrary IFC geometry into simple room polygons and wall segments just to reuse BuildingDescription.

Use common stable object references to connect reasoning records, source evidence and viewer selection.

5. Use this context throughout Q&A

Retrieve question-relevant structured records for the sufficiency gate, reasoning model and post-draft review.

For native IFC:
- Code selects relevant original records.
- Code performs supported counts and calculations.
- Gemini interprets the question and explains results.
- Answers cite the contributing original IFC records and properties.

For drawings:
- Supply the structured interpretation alongside original visual evidence.
- The reviewer must not assess an answer solely against extraction JSON or the answer model’s explanation.

Validate that retrieved context covers the question’s scope. A selected subset must not be mistaken for a complete building-wide inventory.

Unsupported or incomplete calculations must expose their missing inputs and coverage limitations rather than silently returning a complete-looking total.

Preserve source-linked highlighting through shared stable IDs. Uncertain associations retain citations without invented highlights.

BUILDING-MODEL REVIEW LOOP

The building-model loop produces an interactive preview, then improves it through targeted revisions.

For drawings, the pipeline is:

Original drawing
→ building-description JSON
→ deterministic IFC generation
→ reopened geometry
→ interactive model

Genuine uploaded IFCs use direct extraction and rendering. Do not route them through drawing reconstruction or automatically rewrite their original contents.

A reconstruction reviewer examines the original drawing, description and actual generated geometry together. JSON-only review could overlook generator errors or approve a plausible interpretation that does not match the source.

1. Generate the first description and preview.

The implementer describes depicted floors, spaces, walls, openings and meaningful features, retaining source regions and uncertainty.

Deterministic code generates and reopens the IFC. After local validation, publish the first usable model as:

“Preview · review in progress.”

Do not wait for the complete refinement loop before making a usable preview available.

2. Review against the original.

Supply full-page context, relevant crops, the description and original-coordinate overlays derived from the actual reopened IFC.

Check:
- Missing meaningful features.
- Invented walls or floors.
- Wall connectivity and relative thickness.
- Opening placement, width and wall associations.
- Indoor/outdoor boundaries and incorrect enclosure.
- Furnishing and fixture coverage.
- Unsupported dimensions and other assumptions.

The reviewer must examine actual generated geometry, not only the description or attractive concept styling.

3. Return actionable feedback.

Each issue identifies:
- The affected object or original source region.
- The discrepancy.
- Supporting source evidence.
- The proposed inspection or correction.
- Any uncertainty that prevents a confident correction.

For example:

“This boundary crosses the depicted balcony opening. Reinspect this source region and revise the boundary’s classification or extent.”

Distinguish extraction, generation and display problems. If the JSON is correct but the generator renders it incorrectly, do not distort the description to compensate.

4. Apply targeted corrections.

Patch the affected description records while preserving unrelated objects and their identities.

Unsupported or ambiguous interpretations remain unresolved. Do not casually rewrite the entire building on each iteration.

Runtime models propose description corrections. They must not generate or execute Python, raw IFC text or application-code patches.

5. Validate the candidate revision.

Regenerate and reopen the IFC, then check both the requested correction and possible regressions elsewhere.

Review what disappeared as well as what improved. A repair to a balcony must not silently remove a bathroom wall or door.

Keep the previous usable revision if generation fails or a clear regression is found.

6. Publish the update without disrupting exploration.

Prepare replacement geometry offscreen and swap the complete revision into the viewer. Do not expose a partially replaced scene.

Preserve:
- Camera position and orbit target; no automatic fit.
- Selected floor and floor separation where the floor still exists.
- Inspection/concept mode.
- Cutaway and assumption controls.
- Selected object when its identity survives.
- Stable concept decoration placements where supporting geometry is unchanged.

Revalidate answer highlights against the new revision.

If an object is removed or becomes unresolved, explain the change and retain its source evidence. Do not silently select an unrelated replacement.

If the footprint changes substantially, offer “Fit updated model” instead of moving the camera automatically.

STABLE IDENTITIES AND COORDINATES

Object identities must survive insertion and reordering.

Persistent object IDs must map consistently to IFC GlobalIds. List positions cannot serve as enduring identities.

Preserve existing imported artifact IDs and compatibility. New objects receive new IDs; deleted objects must not have their IDs reassigned to unrelated features.

Source-to-display frames must remain stable during ordinary refinement. Changing a floor’s bounding box must not recenter or rescale existing geometry.

Preserve the shared-page scale fix:
- Uncalibrated diagrams on the same page retain their relative drawn proportions.
- This does not establish physical scale or prove that independently resized diagrams use equal drawing scales.
- Relationships across different pages remain schematic unless supported.
- Supported physical calibration remains intact.

Supported calibration or orientation corrections require an explicit transform update.

Use building/revision identifiers on reconstruction updates and QA requests. Reject stale patches and stale asynchronous updates rather than allowing an older job to overwrite a newer revision.

RECONSTRUCTION STOPPING BEHAVIOR

The loop stops when:
- There are no actionable supported corrections.
- Repeated attempts make no material progress.
- The user stops the job.
- An explicitly configured execution budget is reached.

Preserve the best available revision and remaining issues.

Reviewer agreement does not justify a “verified accurate” badge. Unresolved disagreements remain visible.

A model can be available with unresolved issues. Availability and completeness are separate states.

Q&A REVIEW LOOP

The Q&A loop inspects evidence, drafts internally and reviews the answer before publication.

1. Establish the evidence context.

Capture the question and current building revision.

Retrieve relevant reasoning JSON and original evidence through the shared interface.

Keep the input distinction:
- Genuine uploaded IFC: use its actual records, relationships and supported geometry calculations.
- Image/PDF: inspect original pages alongside the structured interpretation.
- Drawing-generated IFC: continue using the original drawing as evidence, including after reopening.

Drawing-generated geometry and concept decorations do not establish factual dimensions.

2. Check evidence sufficiency.

Retain the existing Decisions gate:
- Sufficient: proceed to drafting.
- Insufficient: explain what is missing from the inspected material.
- Unclear: perform the permitted targeted inspection or request clarification; unresolved uncertainty remains explicit.

Missing information is scoped to the inspected material, not asserted to be absent everywhere.

3. Generate an internal draft.

Gemini supplies:
- The proposed answer.
- Source citations.
- Relevant calculation inputs and derivations.
- Explicit limitations.

The draft is not yet presented as the final answer.

4. Run deterministic validation.

Check source references, units and calculations.

Code performs supported native-IFC counts and geometry operations using the actual records, including relevant objects without renderable geometry.

Do not ask the model to replace deterministic counting or arithmetic where the required records and inputs are available.

5. Review the draft against the evidence.

Decisions receives:
- The user’s question.
- The draft answer.
- The original evidence or faithful extracted native-IFC records.
- Relevant structured context with provenance and coverage.
- Calculation results and relevant validation findings.

For drawings, include the necessary original visual evidence. Do not supply only the reconstruction JSON or the answer model’s explanation.

Ask one overall question:

“Does the inspected original evidence support this draft’s answer to the user’s question, including its factual claims and derivations, without treating assumptions as facts?”

Route the result:
- Supported: publish after local validation passes.
- Contradicted: reinspect the evidence and revise.
- Unsupported by inspected evidence: seek missing evidence if available; otherwise explain the limitation.
- Unclear: inspect further or return explicit uncertainty.

Do not introduce a large set of independent model vetoes. Add targeted diagnostic checks only where demonstrated failure modes justify them.

6. Revise through meaningful progress.

Each retry must:
- Inspect additional evidence.
- Correct a calculation.
- Repair a citation.
- Remove an unsupported claim.
- Or narrow the answer appropriately.

Rephrasing the same unsupported assertion until it receives approval is not progress.

Decisions provides a routing judgment, not a written critique. The reasoning model identifies the correction using original evidence and concrete validation failures.

A wrong room count can be corrected. An actual ceiling height absent from the supplied material cannot be recovered through repeated reasoning.

7. Publish with validated associations.

Show the answer, citations, limitations and reliably associated highlights.

Uncertain object mappings retain source evidence without invented highlights. A missing highlight must not suppress an otherwise supported textual answer.

If reconstruction changed during the request, revalidate highlight associations against the displayed revision. Original source citations remain available even if an earlier object mapping no longer works.

During Q&A, show progress such as:
- “Inspecting source.”
- “Checking answer.”

The model remains usable while the answer is prepared. Questions do not automatically trigger reconstruction.

SHARED EVIDENCE BOUNDARIES

- Original IFC records support answers about the supplied model; they are not proof of as-built reality.
- Drawing-derived IFC remains an interpretation, including after export and reopening.
- Unknown scale stays explicitly unscaled.
- Extrusion heights, decorative materials and proposed furnishings remain assumptions.
- Actual-height questions still refuse when the original source supplies no height.
- Concept additions never become factual evidence merely because they are visible.
- API failures are operational errors, not evidence-quality judgments.
- Missing information is scoped to the inspected material.
- Optional similar-building ideas remain explicitly hypothetical proposals.
- A reviewer’s approval is corroboration, not proof of correctness.
- Model confidence must not be presented as measured accuracy on this dataset.
- Dataset ground-truth answers remain evaluation-only and never become runtime context.

INTEGRATE THE EXISTING CONCEPT PRESENTATION

See the verification report for controlled probes and actual live outcomes.\n\nTyped patches preserve existing persistent IDs and require original source evidence. A floor metadata replacement cannot execute implicit nested edits. Its nested copies must preserve base/current ID order and length and exactly match base/current records or separately declared same-floor, same-collection replacements. The floor operation retains staged nested arrays; every separate edit still passes normal source, identity, review and provenance checks. Any invalid operation rejects the entire candidate.\n\nMissing-geometry requests are shared between local detection and both providers. A valid wall segment does not require an optional footprint; already complete geometry is reused. Missing registration applies to non-reference floors only. These requests guide targeted enrichment, not source completeness judgments. Deterministic IFC generation, reopening and original-coordinate overlays support source review. Existing usable geometry is retained on invalid/rejected replacements. A first model can be published as preview while review runs; preview status is not a fidelity guarantee. Concept styling never enters source counts, QA evidence or IFC facts.\n\n## Conversation and reviewed answers\n\n`AskRequest` contains `document_id`, `question` and optional `revision_id`, `request_id`, `conversation_id`, `reply_to`, `clarification_response`. `conversation_id` is the selected building ID. Async repeated `request_id` reuses its question job. History comes from the server's saved building conversation; client-supplied assistant assertions are not accepted as evidence.\n\nMessages carry `id`, `role`, `revision_id`, `timestamp`, optional job/request/reply references, and either user `question` or assistant `answer`. Clarification replies reference an existing assistant clarification in that building. Earlier answers help resolve phrases such as “the upper floor” but remain fallible context, never additional factual sources.\n\nIntent resolution is separate from source sufficiency. A clarification returns:\n\n```json\n{\"status\":\"clarification\",\"answer\":\"Which floor?\",\"clarification\":{\"message\":\"Which floor?\",\"suggestions\":[\"Ground floor\",\"Upper floor\",\"Both\"],\"free_text_allowed\":true},\"gate\":null,\"inspection_passes\":0}\n```\n\nIt has no evidence refusal or reviewed factual draft. Ordinary answers retain `answered|insufficient|unclear`, the three-way sufficiency gate, bounded additional inspection and post-draft review. Answers include `answered_revision_id`, `display_revision_id`, validated original-page `evidence` or native `model_evidence`, conservative `highlight_ids`, `support_summary`, review metadata, and `calculation_results` with source-bound inputs/results. Rejected drafts do not become findings. Chat citations work without 3D and open the exact answered source revision; unreliable geometry associations omit highlights.\n\nDoor questions distinguish depicted symbols from all installed building doors. A schedule is not universally required for visible leaves/swings/jambs. Ambiguous openings should be identified individually and connecting doors counted once. Gate, draft and review all apply these rules; generated object totals cannot replace original drawing inspection.\n\nFor `sources_only` reasoning, nested `user_provided` calibration/registration/stair connection fields are stripped from the serialized interpretation copy and supplied-value records are omitted. Saved data remains unchanged. Permitted `sources_and_user` answers expose relevant inputs separately, cite `user_value_evidence` IDs and receive server-added `user_value_attributions`; original-source questions cannot silently adopt them.\n\n## Editable inputs and provenance\n\nAssumption rows expose `id`, `scope`, `property`, `label`, `value`, `unit`, `provenance`, `reason`, optional `source`, and `editable`. Provenance distinguishes observed information, inferred interpretations, display assumptions, unknowns and user-provided values. Shared floor assumptions are grouped; source observations are retained separately.\n\nThe batch payload is:\n\n```json\n{\"base_revision_id\":\"...\",\"edits\":[{\"property\":\"floor_height\",\"scope\":{\"floor_id\":\"...\"},\"value\":3.4,\"unit\":\"m\",\"reason\":\"Provided by user\"}],\"supporting_source_ids\":[]}\n```\n\nEach edit may also cite `source:{page,bbox,source_id?,source_page?}`. Supporting files must already belong to the building. Implemented properties are:\n\n| Property | Value and scope |\n|---|---|\n| `floor_height` | Finite positive number; floor scope; `m`, `mm`, `cm`, `ft` or `in`. |\n| `display_height` | Positive number; floor scope; physical units above or explicit `relative` display units. |\n| `calibration` | `{length:number,segment:[[x,y],[x,y]]}` with distinct normalized endpoints, physical unit and a source region on the selected floor's page. |\n| `stair_connection` | Selected stair object/floor; `{target_floor_id,target_feature_id?}` referencing another known floor and optionally its stair. |\n| `interpretation_correction` | Nonempty text describing a scoped correction; reviewed through a typed data patch. |\n\nApply validates the full batch before mutation. Inputs retain their IDs, scope, units, source support, submission/base revision and `user_provided` provenance. Observed source heights are not rewritten as user values. Known source calibration/height conflicts, including section observations with uncertain scope, retain both source facts and submitted inputs and return `needs_attention` without replacing the usable revision. Equivalent calibration is compared using original-page aspect and physical unit conversion.\n\nNumeric changes to an existing scene generate/reopen locally, run loss checks and use one existing original-source/actual-geometry review before publication. The reviewer receives user values separately and must distinguish their authority from source observations. Source-only numeric input persistence does not automatically request 3D. Interpretation corrections invoke the bounded typed-patch workflow. Editing/keystrokes make no model calls. Failed/stopped/rejected candidates retain submitted inputs in the persisted job and preserve the prior usable revision.\n\nA supplied vertical height never establishes XY scale. With unknown horizontal calibration, physical height remains attributed in its original unit; vertical presentation uses the disclosed display convention `1 m = 1.2/2.6 relative units`. The scene stays unscaled. This is a display choice, not an inferred building measurement.\n\n## Geometry, formats and portability\n\nOriginal-page coordinates, building registration/elevation and viewer-only exploded spacing remain separate. Supported shared-page registration can use relative units without asserting metres. Stacked mode retains generated storey elevations; exploded mode adds spacing. Continuous schematic stairs preserve supported footprints/connectivity with assumed vertical geometry identified. Optional wall footprints preserve supported tapered/angled shapes; explicit hosts remain required for openings.\n\nNative floors come from supplied IFC storeys and containment. Cutaway is a percentage clipping control: 0% is the floor reference and 100% the full reference height. All-floor mode uses each storey's own reference; missing heights and uncontained geometry use displayed fallback references. Clipping does not shrink walls or move openings. Camera, floor/mode selection and assumptions controls survive accepted updates where identities remain valid.\n\nSVG and DXF use the existing normalized-image pipeline, with preserved original bytes, vector/layout metadata and coordinate mappings. Declared document units alone do not establish physical building scale. Unsupported rendering features are reported; external resources are not fetched. DWG is unavailable because no validated converter path exists. See `SOURCE_FORMATS.md` for adapter details.\n\nPortable artifact v5 adds available original source bytes/hashes, mappings, source interpretations and user inputs; V2–V4 remain readable. Legacy derived artifacts may contain only embedded normalized pages with null source IDs and no recoverable original file bytes. Those pages remain authoritative supplied image evidence; absent original files are never fabricated. Upgrading such an artifact to v5 does not recover missing originals. Original pages and derived status are restored on import. Existing per-file/source normalization and artifact-size limits remain explicit; the PDF five-page bound is not a cumulative building-page or DXF-layout bound. An over-capacity portable export must fail explicitly while preserving the local bundle. Large multi-source exports and complex vector semantics are not guaranteed complete reconstruction.\n# Reconstruction V3 contract (reviewed)\n\nRoot owns shared schema/API/provider and import integration. V3 replaces room-edge enclosure generation with an explicit physical-boundary description. Original-page coordinates, source-only QA, unknown scale and V2 portable imports remain compatible.\n\n## Description\n\nKeep BuildingDescription(floors, limitations) and existing floor source/order/orientation/calibration fields. RoomDescription adds environment indoor|outdoor|unknown; its polygon creates only an IfcSpace footprint, never walls. Add floor.boundaries, floor.features and floor.unresolved. No list caps.\n\nBoundaryDescription: key:str (unique within floor), kind wall|railing|open_edge, label, segment:list[Point], source:PageRegion, thickness_segment:list[Point] (empty if unknown), basis observed|inferred, note. Walls and railings require two segment endpoints; open_edge additionally accepts a continuous polyline rendered as flat strips, never an enclosure. Physical wall records describe one shared wall axis spanning any explicitly hosted gaps; each shared physical boundary is listed once. Thin door leaves, arcs, furniture and annotations are not walls. Explicit railings/open edges never become full-height walls.\n\nOpeningDescription replaces host_room/host_edge with host_wall:str|null (boundary key); retain kind, label, segment, source, basis, note. Segment endpoints identify the actual gap on the wall, not a drawn door leaf or swing arc. Unknown host stays null and yields an unresolved record, never arbitrary attachment. No valid host depends on a room polygon surviving.\n\nFeatureDescription: kind stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other, label, polygon:list[Point], source:PageRegion, basis, note. Every meaningful depicted feature is included, with simple footprint symbols sufficient; no vertical dimension is required. Generic other+label covers features outside the named categories. UnresolvedDescription: label, category:str, source:PageRegion, reason. Use for ambiguous classification or unlocatable geometry; annotations are excluded. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual extents cannot be resolved.\n\n## Scene and IFC\n\nSceneElement adds representation reconstructed|schematic|unresolved, semantic_type:str, environment indoor|outdoor|unknown. Extend kind to room/outdoor/wall/railing/open_edge/door/window/stairs/furniture/fixture/other. Unresolved elements have geometry=None but retain stable GlobalId, source, label and note reason. Every described entry must appear as rendered/schematic/unresolved, including validation omissions. Stable namespace keys must not renumber after omission. No silent omission counter as the only record.\n\nGenerated spaces are thin plates. Explicit walls use depicted thickness where a valid original segment establishes it, otherwise labeled display width. Openings create actual IfcOpeningElement void/fill relationships; host geometry is checked in aspect-correct coordinates. Reject incompatible/overlapping host associations to unresolved records. Never close a room edge to create a host. Features may be flat schematic IFC solids/symbols; any thickness, height, tread motif or vertical offset is a display assumption. No engineering/step-count claims.\n\nNew artifacts use manifest version3/marker v3 and embed the exact BuildingDescription plus all original normalized PNGs and per-element metadata. Reader accepts version2 artifacts without silently reclassifying them as native IFC. Version3 validates new semantic/status fields against per-element Psets, actual IFC classes/storeys and source regions. Unresolved entries use geometry-less semantic entities; all-unresolved scenes are allowed but explicitly state that no 3D geometry was reconstructed; the original source and unresolved inventory remain available. Native IFC import unchanged.\n\n## Comparison UI\n\nRoot provides Scene.comparison: list[PlanComparison] computed after actual IFC tessellation. Each entry: element_id, floor_id, page, layer spaces|walls|openings|features|unresolved, polygons:list[list[list[float]]], lines:list[list[list[float]]], method:str, cut_height:float|null. Coordinates are normalized ORIGINAL page. They are inverse-transformed from actual meshes using stored SceneFloor.transform, without viewer explosion offsets. Walls use a horizontal cross-section through the assumed opening height (explicitly labeled display section), other elements use actual footprint projection. Unresolved entries carry no fabricated paths; UI uses element.source.bbox as a visibly different unresolved marker. Recompute on reopening; do not trust stale saved overlay paths.\n\nFrontend adds a comparison control in the original drawing view, layer toggles and overlay opacity. Original orientation remains unchanged. Separate floor/page filtering, source-linked semantic/status counts and unresolved feature list make missing/incorrect features reviewable. Mesh highlights and assumption controls remain independent. Image-answer association may include new valid feature kinds, but unresolved or unrenderable entries cannot receive invented 3D highlights. Original source citations remain available.\n\n## Budget and acceptance\n\nExisting upload/IFC safeguards remain; no new floor/room/feature caps. Larger explicit inventories may exceed the current reconstruction token/time budget; measure live and change reconstruction-only settings if required, after communicating the tradeoff. No changes to gate/answer budgets or automatic provider fallback.\n\nAcceptance requires visual original-coordinate comparison of both unchanged11397 floors and1794, explicit audit of outdoor boundaries, physical shared walls, every clear opening, stairs and furnishing/fixture coverage, plus live source QA/highlights/refusal and portable reopening. Passing mesh validation alone is not fidelity evidence. Record residual unresolved features/omissions honestly.\n\n## Review resolutions\nDuplicate boundary keys never resolve by first/last wins: all conflicting records and dependent openings remain unresolved. Invalid item geometry never invents an exact source region: retain a valid explicit item region, otherwise use the valid floor region and label it unlocalized; invalid floor/page references fail. An empty mesh set is a source inventory result, not a successful 3D reconstruction. The frontend uses safe empty bounds and a clear no-geometry notice.\n\n## Final implementation settings\n\nReconstruction alone uses one Gemini `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` high-thinking request (explicit `GEMINI_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL` override), 150 seconds and 32,768 output tokens. These are measured hackathon design choices; larger inventories can still fail, and API success is not fidelity acceptance. Answer/crop retain 45 seconds/8,192 tokens; Decisions is unchanged. Temporary OpenAI uses the same reconstruction-only time/token budgets. No automatic fallback, refinement call, manual source edits or new image-processing stage was added.\n\nV3 permits a contextual evidence box to extend beyond its approximate floor region when the same-page boxes overlap with positive area. Actual geometry anchors remain inside both the floor and source region; no source box is silently rewritten. Disjoint/wrong-page regions remain unresolved. V2 portable imports retain their prior containment check.\n\nRoom interiors with positive overlap remain unresolved rather than being silently repaired; independent walls/openings/features survive. Empty feature polygons explicitly request a bbox schematic, while malformed supplied polygons remain unresolved. Display stair bands are level symbol marks, never measured tread counts, rise or travel direction.\n\n## Boundary-line citation repair\n\nBoundaryDescription.source now uses BoundaryRegion: area or normalized positive-length line. Other PageRegion/QA contracts remain strict. A line citation must contain the actual boundary segment before the generator adds one-original-page-pixel selection padding to the zero dimension; physical geometry and thickness validation use original coordinates. Original line bounds remain embedded in the exact description; the padded SourceRef carries a selection-only note. Inconsistent associations remain unresolved. See RECONSTRUCTION_502_FIX.md.\n\n## Shared uncalibrated page scale\n\nUncalibrated floor transforms use a page-derived factor `10/max(page.width/page.height,1)` rather than independently normalizing each floor bbox. Floor boxes affect centering only. This preserves drawn proportions among uncalibrated diagrams on one page; it does not prove physical scale or equal drawing scales, especially for independently resized diagrams. Separate page frames remain schematic. Supported physical calibration is unchanged. New `page_extent` assumptions disclose the convention; the UI checks those markers before making the claim. Existing artifacts retain stored transforms and original IDs; no automatic migration. See FLOOR_SCALE_FIX.md.\n\n## Depicted wall bands and schematic visibility\n\nA supplied boundary segment is a reference line, not necessarily a centerline. A valid perpendicular thickness segment establishes signed face offsets in the aspect-correct source plane. Validate contact before display rotation; extrude between those faces. This retains depicted relative widths at unknown scale. Missing/invalid widths keep explicit display defaults. Supported band contacts form junctions without endpoint snapping or filling positive gaps.\n\nOpening range and normal-offset checks use the same source plane and named host. Gap endpoints retain their longitudinal positions. Void and fill are centered normally within the supported band (or assumed default band), with an explicit placement assumption; voids cut the full band. A previously accepted opening outside the actual supported band is not grandfathered in.\n\nFeature footprints and source classifications remain fallible drawing interpretations. Raised schematics improve visibility without establishing vertical measurements. Relative to the existing assumed wall height H, display heights are table .30H; chair/bed .20H; sofa/sink/toilet .25H; cabinet .50H; appliance .40H; shower/bath/stairs/other .10H. Motifs and dimensions are portable assumptions. Support symbols do not establish leg counts; chair facing and stair ascent/rise/travel direction are not inferred. New geometry must remain inside the existing footprint.\n\nUnresolved canvas annotations are HTML source links, not IFC geometry or answer highlights. Precise source regions use the stored source transform; coarse/unlocalized records use a labeled floor badge. Annotation screen positions may be separated for legibility without changing source coordinates or exported geometry. A more elevated derived-model camera exposes interiors; native IFC camera behavior is unchanged. See SCHEMATIC_FIDELITY_PLAN.md and SCHEMATIC_FIDELITY_RESULTS.md.\n"}

# Source-first iteration implementation plan

Status: independently reviewed and approved in round 1; no planning blockers. Reviewer explicitly confirmed source/revision compatibility, optional geometry, unknown-scale supplied heights, cached append, artifact portability and actual-IFC elevation requirements. This plan implements all twelve authoritative attachment requirements; it supersedes older single-source, automatic-reconstruction, new-format exclusion and no-commit instructions where the newer user request differs. Gemini and its configurable reconstruction model remain unchanged. Focused milestone commits are authorized; pushes are not.

## Scope and design choices

Keep the existing one-process FastAPI, plain browser JavaScript, filesystem bundles, original evidence, shared description, deterministic IfcOpenShell generator, reviewed QA and concept renderer. Add automatic source interpretation, explicitly requested optional geometry, incremental multi-source buildings, source-linked conversation/clarification, editable attributed values, coherent floor presentation, diagnostics and a separate format adapter track. Preserve V2–V4 artifacts and saved bundles.

No arbitrary source/object/vertex cap is proposed. Existing per-file normalization/provider/job limits remain visible and must be reported individually; do not reinterpret the historical five-page per-file bound as a five-page whole-building bound. Existing 25 MiB portable IFC bound may prevent embedding large multi-source sets: report that export limitation without losing the local bundle or blocking QA. Existing configured correction/call budgets remain; extraction alone must not spend reconstruction-review/repair calls. Root must communicate any necessary changed budget before live calls. Local resource isolation for SVG/DXF protects the renderer from active content/external resources; it can reject drawings relying on external assets, so report unsupported features explicitly. These are implementation choices, not claims about source validity.

Exclude detailed roofs/domes, photorealism, Blender/cloud rendering, auth/database and autonomous runtime agents. Unknown geometry stays unresolved. SVG and DXF are now included; DWG support depends on an actually verified converter and must never be advertised speculatively.

## Evidence from current implementation

- `BuildingStore.add` uses original SHA256 as building ID and one building-level source/pages manifest; immutable revision files do not yet pin source membership.
- `reconstruct_scene` saves description only after generate/reopen. `build_reasoning` derives drawing objects/floors from scene rather than interpretation.
- `JobRunner` combines extraction, geometry and review, with generic failure text implying an earlier model even on first failure.
- Existing stable IDs, frame registries, atomic CURRENT publication, candidate retention, original-page overlays and source-only drawing QA are reusable.
- `generate_ifc` explicitly gives every floor elevation zero; metric-only alignment disallows supported registration of unscaled diagrams. The viewer already adds an independent exploded offset but cannot repair missing building elevation.
- Existing `segment` plus thickness-band walls cannot faithfully represent every tapered/angled end. Diagnose actual outputs before choosing schema or generator corrections.

## Shared contracts (freeze before dependent implementation)

### Source identity and revision membership

A building keeps its existing 64-hex `building_id` (initial source hash); adding files never changes it. A `source_id` is SHA256 of original bytes, independent of filename. Source metadata includes original bytes/hash, display filename aliases, media kind, normalized page hashes/dimensions, normalization mapping/diagnostics and optional vector metadata. Deduplicate resources and successful interpretation by source identity, including reuse across buildings; do not reuse a source result conditioned on another building's context as independent extraction.

Each immutable revision saves a `sources` manifest. Entries map `(source_id, source_page)` to an append-only building `page` number, with the original normalized page pixels and coordinate mapping. Never renumber earlier pages. Internal `Page` and public page descriptors add `source_id`, `source_page` and source filename; existing `page` remains the canonical legacy selector. A source extraction cache uses source-local pages; merge explicitly remaps every source reference into the building page namespace and assigns building-stable object IDs. Geometry/review caches are keyed to their input revision, not merely original file hash.

References retain existing `{page,bbox}` and add optional `source_id`/`source_page`; server resolves legacy refs against that revision's manifest and rejects conflicting combinations. Every normalized bbox remains in the displayed original page frame, never the building frame. New evidence URLs are revision-pinned; existing unversioned routes remain compatibility/current routes. An older answer resolves its own source manifest, not CURRENT's source list. Legacy bundles synthesize one source entry on load without rewriting old revisions.

Native IFC keeps original GlobalId/property evidence per `source_id`; model record identity must include source identity when different IFCs repeat a GlobalId. Drawing-derived IFC restores drawing sources and cannot enter native factual shortcuts. Multi-source drawing ingestion is the main UI flow; mixed/native source catalogs retain per-record evidence rules rather than converting native objects to floor polygons. Never silently overwrite or fuse conflicting source facts.

### Shared interpretation with optional geometry

Extend `BuildingDescription` additively, not with a second incompatible reasoning pipeline. Retain floors, original labels, source refs and existing persistent IDs. Allow semantic records without geometric traces: empty/absent polygon/segment fields mean geometry unavailable, not empty evidence. Add source-linked observations/measurements for all view types, including section/elevation facts; only actual floor plans instantiate floor geometry. Expose extraction coverage and per-source completion. Preserve exact returned validated interpretation before any generator call.

Provider interface: `extract_interpretation(document, *, include_geometry=False)` returns the shared schema. The source-first prompt requests useful semantic observations, view classification, labels, measurements and evidence regions without exhaustive wall/feature polygon tracing. Geometry action reuses that interpretation and requests only missing geometry/relationships through the same schema and typed patch workflow; existing full descriptions require no re-extraction. Existing `reconstruct` may remain a compatibility wrapper. Reasoning object/floor records derive from saved interpretation independent of scene; optional scene associations enrich them without becoming factual evidence.

Source extraction operates independently per new source so adding B does not re-extract A. Building integration combines cached source interpretations deterministically; repeated views of a floor must not silently create additional storeys. Merge only source-supported floor equivalences, retain all supporting refs, and mark uncertain alternatives/conflicting dimensions explicitly. Explicit geometry/refinement can inspect multiple originals for cross-source relationships/conflicts. Persist interpretation identity/provenance and missing geometry; no geometry work or reconstruction review on default extraction. Missing interpretation records never establish missing source objects.

Revision payload adds `interpretation_status`, `geometry_status`, and `geometry_revision_id` where retained geometry belongs to an older interpretation. QA pins the current source/interpretation revision; UI explicitly identifies any retained older model, and highlights only validated associations. Publication of extraction must never relabel an older scene as regenerated against new evidence. Successful JSON survives a geometry error, restart or stop. Source-only revisions are first-class successes.

### Jobs, atomicity and APIs

Keep current routes. `POST /api/documents` accepts existing `file` and additive multi-file `files`; source-first upload queues automatic extraction server-side for genuinely uncached drawing sources. `POST /api/buildings/{id}/sources` adds related files to the selected building. Return source list, per-source statuses, extraction job IDs, revision identity and `has_scene`. A duplicate upload/reopen returns cached state without inference; interrupted or failed extraction requires an explicit retry, not surprise reprocessing.

Add `POST /api/buildings/{id}/extraction` for explicit retry. Existing reconstruction endpoint is the explicit Generate 3D/Refine action. Coalesce repeated requests for the same source/operation. Persist source additions before launching inference. Workers extract against immutable source snapshots and save cache results even if their publication base became stale. Under the store lock, merge an unchanged per-source result into the newest source manifest; if related interpretation/user values changed, preserve the candidate and require a deliberate rebase/review. Geometry/refinement still uses compare-and-swap on base revision. No worker may drop newly appended sources or user edits. Stop/restart guards prevent late publication.

Job diagnostics persist `phase`, safe `error_stage`, `error_category`, opaque diagnostic ID, usage and whether a prior model actually exists. Stages distinguish ingestion, extraction provider, interpretation validation, geometry enrichment, IFC generation, reopening and review. Save returned structured outputs privately for deterministic replay; never log raw requests, credentials, source content or provider exception strings. First-model failure says sources/interpretation were saved and no model was generated; only say retained model when one exists.

### Conversation and clarification

Persist conversation messages within the building bundle, each with ID, role, timestamp, input/question, revision, job ID and final result. `AskRequest` adds optional `conversation_id`, `reply_to` and structured `clarification_response`; old callers remain supported. Client sends a message reference, not untrusted assistant evidence. Server retrieves relevant prior turns and explicit selected scope as fallible conversational context; originals and current revision provide factual support.

Question jobs may complete with a distinct typed `clarification` result `{message, suggestions, free_text_allowed:true, reply_to}` rather than an `insufficient` answer. Resolve materially ambiguous intent before the evidence gate, using a small provider intent-routing response; do not impose clarification when a stated reasonable scope suffices. Reuse existing question execution budget and expose this call in usage. Source insufficiency remains the three-way sufficiency gate. Clarification replies preserve intent context without treating earlier assistant assertions as sources.

Final answers retain reviewed status, original citations, native records, calculations, uncertainty and review outcome. UI shows meaningful phases and an expandable Evidence and checks view, never private chain-of-thought or unreviewed drafts. Chat citations load the answered revision's source even without 3D; conservative object links respect current view and preserve camera/orbit. Old messages remain accessible after revision changes and restart.

### Editable attributed inputs

Add immutable revision `user_values` records with ID, scope `{floor_id?,object_id?}`, property, typed value/unit, provenance `user_provided`, optional original evidence/source document ref, reason, base revision and submission identity. Shared assumption rows are computed/grouped by scope+property; distinguish `observed`, `inferred`, `display_assumption`, `unknown`, `user_provided` without changing observed source facts in place. A supplied height never calibrates XY. With unknown horizontal scale, retain the actual supplied height and unit for attributed QA, keep the scene unscaled, and disclose the separate display conversion used for vertical presentation; never treat relative plan units as metres.

`GET /api/buildings/{id}/assumptions` returns grouped rows and editable property descriptors. `POST /api/buildings/{id}/refinements` accepts `{base_revision_id, edits:[...], supporting_source_ids?:[...]}` and returns a job. Validate finite values, supported unit dimensions, scope, source refs and revision before publication; reject executable/arbitrary paths. Supported properties cover storey display/known height, source-referenced plan calibration, stair connectivity and source-linked interpretation corrections through typed patches. Ambiguous corrections remain reviewable inputs, not assumed facts. Do not silently ignore unsupported properties.

Apply and refine persists submitted provenance, assesses source conflicts, changes affected deterministic geometry or uses bounded targeted model review where interpretation is required, then atomically publishes accepted updates. Failed candidates retain submitted values/diagnostics separately plus the prior usable revision. No call on editing/keystrokes. Exports/reopen preserve user values, edits and source identity in additive versioned artifact metadata with V2–V4 readers retained. The new artifact manifest also embeds original source bytes with hash/media kind, normalized pages and source-local mappings/vector metadata, so reopening preserves supplied SVG/DXF originals as well as visual evidence. Existing artifact-size validation remains; if the portable artifact cannot contain these sources, report that export as unavailable while retaining the complete local bundle rather than exporting provenance loss. QA can use user values with explicit attribution for appropriate questions, but drawing-only height questions still refuse unsupported source facts.

### Geometry and viewer

Keep three transforms separate: original page→local floor plane, local floor→building placement/elevation, and viewer-only exploded spacing. Preserve frozen source frames and shared-page scale. Permit supported registration in an unscaled common page frame without asserting metres: matching stair/exterior anchors with inspected evidence can establish translation/rotation; never independently scale floors or equalize footprints. Cross-page scale uncertainty remains explicit. Add source-linked registration/stair relationships with status and provenance; unsupported registration stays schematic.

Generate real storey elevations from supported values or explicitly attributed display spacing in the appropriate display unit. Stacked mode retains them; exploded mode adds spacing. Stair connectivity can use a continuous schematic ramp/flight between established storeys while recording unknown rise/vertical dimensions. Preserve source footprints and the larger terrace; do not introduce a connection from similarity alone. Export/reopen retains base elevation, relation and provenance. Source overlays inverse-transform actual reopened geometry, including building placement, to original coordinates.

Native scene floors derive from supplied storeys/containment even when storeys have no geometry. Missing/ambiguous containment remains visible without inventing a floor. Replace cutaway boolean with 0–100 slider: each selected floor uses its base elevation and supported height, or labeled display reference. In all-floor mode apply the same percentage independently to each storey's reference; uncontained geometry uses an explicitly displayed scene-wide reference. Use clipping planes in inspection and concept modes; do not rescale walls or move openings. Preserve percent, floor, mode, camera and selections across revision swaps.

Investigate wall/opening failures using retained descriptions, host keys, source segments, signed wall bands, transforms and actual reopened meshes. Structured local consistency findings identify duplicate/conflicting hosts, contradictory floor/stair relations, invalid projections and missing geometry, with source refs; they guide source review, not automatic nearest-wall snapping. If actual tapered walls need a richer representation, add optional source footprint polygons to the existing wall record and deterministic extrusion/void logic, retaining segment/band compatibility. Use real source evidence to distinguish extraction error from generator/display error.

## Work packages and ownership

1. **Root integration/backend:** `app/documents.py`, `bundles.py`, `building.py`, `schemas.py`, `reasoning.py`, `source_context.py`, `jobs.py`, `main.py`, `provider.py`, `openai_provider.py`, `service.py`, `revisions.py`, `identities.py`; related backend tests and integration docs. Own source contracts/cache, extraction split, source refs, conversation/user values, safe diagnostics, prompt budgets and artifact version coordination.
