Distinguish counting doors depicted in the supplied plans from establishing every installed door in the actual building. A door schedule is not a universal prerequisite for counting visible symbols.

Return a supported count with source regions when possible. Identify genuinely ambiguous openings individually and explain whether they affect the total. Avoid double-counting a connecting door from its two adjacent spaces. Preserve appropriate uncertainty rather than forcing an exact answer.

This must work from original drawings even when reconstruction fails. Generated IFC object counts must never substitute for factual drawing inspection. Add positive door-count and genuinely ambiguous-opening regression cases; keep evaluation annotations out of runtime context.

5. Provide consistent native IFC floor controls and adjustable cutaway

For duplex_arc.ifc, expose floor selection using supplied storeys and containment relationships. Native IFC should receive the relevant inspection controls already available for generated models.

Replace the binary cutaway with a percentage slider. Define its reference clearly—for example, 0% at the selected storey’s floor level and 100% at full storey height—and make all-floor behavior understandable. Clip geometry rather than shrinking walls or moving openings. Any unsupported reference height remains a display assumption.

6. Assemble drawing-derived floors into one coherent building

For unchanged colorful-11397.png, investigate the lateral offset and the collapse of floors into one plane when vertical separation is disabled.

Separate original page coordinates, building placement and exploded-view offsets. The diagrams’ positions on the sheet must not automatically determine their positions in the building.

Use supported shared features, especially the staircase and exterior boundaries, to register corresponding floors. Preserve their differing footprints, including the larger terrace. Do not independently rescale floors or force equal footprints.

Stacked mode should retain storey elevations; exploded mode should add extra spacing. Where heights are unknown, use explicit display assumptions without presenting them as measured dimensions. Preserve the shared-page scale fix and keep uncertain cross-page scale relationships explicit.

Corresponding stairs should connect the storeys where the source supports that relationship. A simple continuous schematic connection is sufficient; missing rise measurements should not erase clearly depicted connectivity. Preserve supported footprints and label assumed vertical geometry.

7. Diagnose wall shapes and unresolved hosted openings

Inspect the actual description, host associations, transforms and reopened IFC behind messages such as:

> Opening cannot be projected within its explicit host band and original source region.

Determine whether the extraction selected the wrong host, misplaced a wall/opening, misrepresented thickness or introduced inconsistent coordinates. Clear source doorways should prompt correction of the responsible records, not arbitrary attachment to a nearby wall.

Compare the red wall overlays against the actual black wall footprints. The source contains genuinely thick and tapered/angled wall ends; do not assume every unusual shape is erroneous or replace all walls with constant-width rectangles.

Use building-level consistency checks to identify contradictions in walls, openings, storeys and stairs. These checks should guide source inspection and correction, without inventing a “perfect” building from unsupported information.

8. Allow multiple source files for one building

Support uploading several related blueprints together and adding sources to an existing building. Use a suitable kit_institute dataset example if available.

Plans, sections and elevations should contribute their supported information without every view becoming a floor. Preserve file identity, original page coordinates, citations and source-specific authority. Expose conflicting measurements or uncertain alignment.

The user’s selected building and source content should establish grouping; filename similarity can suggest it. Keep this lean: extend the existing building bundle and reasoning representation rather than introducing a new subsystem.

Preserve building-type agnosticism, original labels, neutral concept styling, stable IDs, portable provenance, source-based QA, refusals, conservative highlights and independent assumption controls. Gemini remains the final-demo provider; keep the provider switch and current model default.

Verify the changed flows using colorful-34.png, colorful-11397.png, colorful-1794.png, native duplex IFC and a related non-residential document set. Include live Gemini checks, original-coordinate overlays, actual reopened geometry, restart/reupload reuse and independent browser review. Report remaining fidelity gaps honestly.

Before introducing new constraints, explain what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are external requirements or design choices, and how they could block valid inputs or the demo. Defer photorealism, detailed roofs/domes, new formats, Blender, cloud rendering and unrelated infrastructure.

9. Turn the right-hand panel into a source-linked QA conversation

Replace the isolated question/result interaction with a lightweight chat scoped to the selected building. Preserve conversation context so follow-up questions such as “What about the upper floor?” can resolve their references.

When ambiguity materially changes the answer, Gemini should ask a brief clarification, preferably with selectable suggestions and a free-text option. For example:

> “Do you mean the ground floor, upper floor, or both?”

Distinguish unclear user intent from insufficient source evidence. Asking for clarification should not appear as a refusal. Avoid unnecessary clarification when a reasonable interpretation can be stated clearly in the answer.

Show meaningful progress and an expandable Evidence and checks view containing:

- Inspected blueprint regions or original IFC records.
- Supported calculations and their inputs.
- A concise explanation of what supports the answer.
- Remaining uncertainty and review outcome.

This should expose useful, evidence-based explanations rather than promise a stream of the model’s private internal reasoning. Do not present unreviewed drafts as final findings.

Citations and object references should connect the conversation to the left-hand viewer. Blueprint references open the original file/page/region; reliable model associations highlight corresponding objects. Respect the selected view and preserve camera controls. If an object mapping is uncertain or 3D is unavailable, the source citation must still work.

Keep original evidence authoritative throughout follow-ups. Earlier assistant messages and extracted JSON are fallible context, not new factual sources. Associate answers with their building revision and preserve access to the evidence used for older answers.

10. Add an editable assumptions and missing-information panel

Provide a clean, source-linked table for reconstruction assumptions and unresolved inputs. Distinguish:

- Information observed in the supplied sources.
- Inferred interpretations.
- Display assumptions.
- Unknown information.
- Values supplied by the user.

Group shared assumptions—such as a floor’s display height—rather than presenting hundreds of duplicate rows. Each editable entry should identify the affected floor/object, property, current value or unknown state, units, and why the value was assumed. Selecting an entry should locate its source region and associated geometry where available.

Allow users to provide missing information or correct an interpretation, with an optional supporting document or source region. For example, they could supply a storey height, a known plan distance for calibration, or clarify a stair connection.

User-provided information must retain its provenance. A supplied height should be labeled “provided by user,” not silently converted into a dimension observed in the blueprint. QA may use it with explicit attribution when appropriate; questions about what the drawing itself establishes must retain that distinction. A known vertical height must not automatically establish horizontal plan scale.

Let users edit several entries and submit them through an explicit Apply and refine action. Do not make model calls on every keystroke. Applying changes should:

1. Validate values, units, scope and revision.
2. Preserve the submitted information with its provenance.
3. Review conflicts with existing sources.
4. Refine affected geometry using the existing bounded workflow.
5. Retain the previous usable revision if the candidate fails.
6. Publish an accepted update without resetting exploration.

Preserve user-provided values and their attribution through saving, export and reopening. This is structured input to deterministic generation—not permission to execute user- or model-generated code.

Verify clarification and follow-up QA without any 3D model, clickable chat evidence in both views, and a user-supplied reconstruction value producing a traceable revision. Unsupported source-height questions must still refuse when the original drawing supplies no height, even if a display assumption or user-provided value is available.


11. Evaluate generalization continuously using previously unseen inputs

Do not optimize the pipeline around a closed list of demo images. Keep known failures as regression tests, and regularly evaluate fresh examples at meaningful implementation milestones—particularly after changes to extraction prompts, schemas, geometry generation or QA.

Vary the inputs across:

- Residential, commercial, institutional and religious buildings.
- Clean drawings, scans, handwritten annotations and sparse plans.
- Rotated diagrams, irregular footprints, multiple floors and multiple related files.
- Dimensioned and unscaled drawings.
- Floor plans, sections, elevations and mixed drawing sets.
- Native IFC and drawing-derived IFC, preserving their different evidence rules.

Select examples from different buildings, not merely different pages or versions of buildings already tested. Maintain a rotating held-out sample. Once a failure informs an implementation change, retain it as a regression case and choose new unseen examples for subsequent generalization checks.

Use the same application pipeline for every case. Avoid filename-specific behavior, hardcoded coordinates, building-specific prompts or manually repaired artifacts presented as successful extraction. Dataset reference answers remain evaluation-only.

Evaluate stages separately:

- Source ingestion and structured extraction.
- Useful QA before or without 3D.
- Grounded answers, appropriate clarification and unnecessary refusals.
- Geometry fidelity, floor relationships, openings and feature coverage.
- Provenance, caching, refinement and recovery from failures.
- Latency and token usage.

Include direct visual comparisons and independent browser inspection. Successful API calls, valid IFC files and higher object counts do not establish fidelity.

Use representative live checks within explicitly communicated budgets rather than rerunning the entire dataset after every edit. Report the selection, failures and limitations so demo-case success cannot conceal broader weaknesses.

The goal is robust handling of arbitrary inputs within the supported formats and documented limits. Complete reconstruction will not always be justified. When information is missing or a view cannot be reconstructed reliably, the pipeline should still preserve usable evidence, answer supported questions, identify unresolved portions and request targeted clarification where useful. It should neither crash generically nor invent a complete building.

12. Add remaining file formats through an independent implementation track

Assign a dedicated subagent an isolated worktree, with agreed interfaces and file ownership, so format support can progress alongside the core work. Integrate through independent review. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.

Start with SVG:

Original SVG → normalized source image
             → shared reasoning JSON
             → QA and optional 3D

Preserve the original vector file, text, proportions and coordinate mapping. Citations, overlays and source inspection must remain traceable to the supplied drawing. SVG coordinates and document dimensions must not automatically establish physical building scale.

Render SVG into the existing source-preview pipeline rather than embedding raw SVG directly in the browser. Report unsupported rendering features explicitly.

Then extend to DXF, preserving relevant layers, units and source references where available. Assess the actual available DWG conversion path before claiming support; any dependency or availability limitation should remain explicit and should not block SVG or other development.

Use matching SVG/PDF examples from the institute dataset for comparison, plus previously unseen examples. Verify labels, linework, proportions, source coordinates, QA, caching and optional reconstruction—not merely successful file loading.

# Progressive source-grounded building product

The active specification is [PRODUCT_SPEC.md](PRODUCT_SPEC.md). It supersedes older exclusions of persistence, background jobs and review loops. Preserve the current configurable reconstruction model; Hydrogen was not adopted. No general-purpose agent runtime, database, external rendering service or new dependencies.

## Reviewed checkpoints and ownership

1. Frontend ports the existing concept renderer selectively from the read-only concept worktree. Keep current inspection fixes. Add source/proposal picking and disclosure, footprint containment/fallback, a keyed decoration ledger, offscreen preparation and atomic viewer swaps. Preserve camera, target, modes, floor, separation, cutaway, assumptions and surviving selections. Never mutate reasoning/export data.
2. Root owns filesystem building bundles, content identity, immutable revisions, CAS publication, stable object IDs and frozen source frames. Store original bytes/pages, descriptions/native records, reasoning, IFC, scene, mappings, assumptions, findings and pipeline metadata. Restore existing artifact IDs and exact descriptions. New server-owned IDs survive insertion/reordering; deleted IDs are tombstoned.
3. Backend owns shared reasoning and native IFC extraction: complete semantic identity catalog including geometry-less objects, properties/quantities/units, supplied relationships, explicitly calculated summaries, missing/coverage records and original references. Drawings keep fallible interpretations plus original visual evidence; generated IFC never becomes native factual evidence.
4. Root owns the lightweight background runner/API; backend owns model review/patch hooks and actual-IFC overlay images. Publish initial usable preview before review, accept only targeted source-supported patches, reopen candidate geometry, audit disappeared/unresolved objects and review regressions. Preserve best revision on failure, stop, stale result, no progress or budget exhaustion.
5. Backend owns reviewed QA: pinned revision, relevant structured/source context, existing sufficiency gate, internal draft, deterministic references/units/calculations, one four-way Decisions support judgment, one meaningful repair and second review if necessary. No published unreviewed claim or repeated paraphrase-until-approval. Root integrates asynchronous progress and final highlight revalidation; frontend keeps exploration usable.
6. Root integrates all acceptance flows; independent reviewer checks code and directly uses browser/original overlays. Separate live inference from fixtures and report source-fidelity failures without hiding earlier usable artifacts.

Planner and independent reviewer approved checkpoint 1 and the full plan after one clarification round. Reviewers do not implement their own reviewed paths. Root owns contracts/commits. Frontend owns static files and focused browser tests; backend owns reasoning, review schemas, provider adapters, QA service and focused tests. Existing unrelated worktrees/untracked files remain untouched.

## Shared contracts

- `Document` pins original `source_bytes`, pages, `description`, JSON `reasoning`, building/revision identifiers, monotonic revision number, identity/frame registries and transient question context. `snapshot()` deep-copies interpretation/context and shares immutable source bytes/pages.
- `Scene` retains old fields and adds optional building/revision/parent identifiers, monotonic `revision_number`, and `review_status`. UUID identifiers are never ordered. Viewer candidates capture the current base; stale commits fail. Polling may skip intermediate revisions, so a new scene need not have the displayed revision as its immediate parent.
- All description records gain optional server-managed `persistent_id`. New initial/inserted IDs are assigned by code, never trusted from the model. Existing imported IDs survive migration; immutable target IDs and tombstones prevent reassignment. New artifacts persist identities/frames with a versioned manifest; old artifacts remain readable.
- Ordinary bbox edits do not alter stored floor transforms. Supported orientation/calibration changes require explicit source-backed transform updates. Page-relative scale and cross-page schematic status remain intact.
- `review_reconstruction(document, description, scene, previous_description=None, previous_scene=None, previous_review=None)` examines original full pages/regions plus actual reopened-IFC overlays. Findings identify stable IDs/source, discrepancy, category, evidence, action and uncertainty.
- `patch_reconstruction(document, description, scene, review)` returns a base-revision-bound list of typed add/replace/remove record operations with source evidence and reasons; never executable code. Floor replacement cannot rewrite nested collections. Candidate review and local disappearance/source checks must pass before CAS publication.
- `review_answer(document, question, draft, gate, crop, validation=...)` returns supported/contradicted/unsupported/unclear. `revise_answer(...)` must add actual evidence, repair a bound calculation/citation or narrow/remove unsupported claims. Same-assertion rephrasing is not progress. A model reviewer corroborates, never certifies accuracy.
- Native reasoning may reference storeys/openings/relationships absent from render meshes. Citation validation uses faithful reasoning records; highlighting uses conservative source associations. Complete object catalog, selected context coverage, property coverage and geometry availability are separate states. Calculations resolve source values and units in code; missing inputs never become a complete total.

## Explicit operating budgets

Communicated as design choices, not external limits: background reconstruction call 300 seconds / 65,536 output tokens, whole job 900 seconds, at most two targeted patch attempts; reconstruction review 120 seconds / 16,384 tokens. QA total 180 seconds, existing 45-second per-call ceiling clamped to remaining time, at most two post-draft reviews and one meaningful correction, retaining one targeted unclear inspection. Configuration can change these limits explicitly; exhaustion means processing stopped, not source insufficiency. No new floor/room/vertex/feature caps. Existing upload/IFC safeguards remain unless separately justified.

## Acceptance audit

Every requirement in PRODUCT_SPEC remains in scope. Track live versus fixture evidence for: concept integration and safe proposals; restart/repeat-upload reopening without inference; stable ID/coordinate insertion/reorder; preview during review; source-backed correction; rejected regression; atomic no-camera-reset replacement and retained controls; stale job/patch/QA handling; source/assumption portability; genuine IFC JSON/count/property/relationship/geometry coverage including geometry-less objects and incomplete totals; drawing QA citations/highlights; actual-height refusal; meaningful post-draft repair/uncertainty; before/after original overlays for both unchanged examples; comparative QA outcomes, usage and latency; real browser performance and software limitations; focused commits and reproducible saved-building demo.

Architecture or mocked success alone is not completion. Preserve known fidelity limitations and failed live experiments. Finish only after integrated verification and no unreported blocking review findings.

Root owns the shared coordination record at `/tmp/junction-ui-coordination.md`. Implementation starts after planning blockers and shared API ownership are settled.

Open on a quiet chat with blueprint attachments using the exact light/dark tokens from `Programmercloud-cmd/AI_Chronicle_UI`, `src/web/styles/global.css` blob `4396f7a3594369ea3a38c6c0ebdb620496f9703c`. Theme switching is conversational, with system preference as the initial choice.

Reuse saved originals, interpretation, source-grounded QA, reconstruction jobs, reviewed attributed-input batches, stable identities, Three.js inspection/concept and portable IFC. Do not replace provider/gate/review/persistence/generation pipelines or modify the other worktrees. No new renderer, model, format, runtime agent framework, dependencies, arbitrary object caps or expanded inference budgets. | Owner | Paths and responsibility |
|---|---|
| Planner | This plan only; revisions in response to independent review. |
| Root/integration | Final action contract, coordination file, additive `app/chat_actions.py`, narrow registration in `app/main.py`, route/schema tests, integration and focused commits. No edits to provider modules owned by the reliability session. |
| UI implementer | `app/static/index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`, optional small `chat-workspace.js`, and focused chat browser tests. Preserve existing operation adapters and render data as text. |

| Independent reviewers | Read-only plan/implementation review, directly operate Chromium, save findings outside implementation files. Never review their own implementation as independent evidence. |

Planner and reviewer operate first; UI/viewer work may run in parallel only after shared signatures settle. Root resolves integration conflicts. Keep provider configuration and requirements unchanged. Reuse the existing Python environment read-only if needed; isolated test stores and ports avoid touching running demo stores.

## Small action/result contract

`POST /api/chat/actions` is an additive intent/validation route, not another job runner. Input: `message`, `request_id`, optional `document_id` and interpretation `revision_id`, plus a captured `workspace`. Output echoes request/document/revision identity and returns `status: ready|clarification`, `actions`, a brief non-factual `message`, and optional focused clarification/suggestions. Existing endpoints execute accepted operations; their results and errors update chat/workspace. The root-owned coordination proposal is authoritative for final operation names; the list below states required capabilities, not competing enum spellings. Root will freeze exact enums in `docs/CHAT_UI_CONTRACT.md` before dependent implementation.

Workspace explicitly stores document/building ID, interpretation revision, displayed geometry revision, view mode (`chat|source|model|concept`), selected IDs, focused ID, camera position/up/target, tour ordered IDs/index/running state, navigation highlighting, answer highlighting and assumption visibility. Also retain floor filter, separation, cutaway and source page/region where applicable. Document revision and geometry revision are distinct because a newer source interpretation can retain older usable geometry.

Use a strict discriminated action schema, with deterministic execution in declared order:

- `show_model` (reuse saved scene; existing reconstruction only when needed), `show_source`, `close_workspace`, `set_camera` (top/front/isometric/fit), `select` (validated IDs), `tour` (start/pause/resume/next/previous), `set_visibility` (answer highlights, navigation highlights, assumptions), `set_view` (inspection/concept), `set_floor`, `set_separation`, `set_cutaway`, `set_theme`.
- `question` forwards the original question and pinned context to the existing reviewed QA route; no factual answer is synthesized by the action interpreter.
- `refine` contains a validated existing `RefinementRequest` batch. Preserve exact user value, unit, scope, source support and attribution; route corrections through `interpretation_correction`. A bare request to improve the existing model uses existing reconstruction `mode: refine`.
- `list_saved`, `open_saved`, `attach_sources`, `new_upload`, `download_ifc`, `download_source`, `retry_extraction`, `stop_job`, `refresh`, `inspect_assumptions`, `inspect_inventory`, `set_comparison` cover existing application operations without separate settings/toolbars. File choice/download still uses browser-native controls reached through chat. Ambiguous saved building, floor, source, job or refinement scope requests a focused choice.

Gemini (or the explicitly configured OpenAI adapter) interprets language once using existing structured transport through an additive adapter. The prompt requests intent and reference selectors, never authoritative facts or fabricated IDs. Supply saved semantic labels/IDs/kinds/floors and current workspace context; no screenshot rediscovery or raw source image pass is needed for navigation. Code resolves `focused`, `selection`, named IDs/labels, kinds and floors against the correct saved revision, validating membership, renderability and source evidence. Duplicate labels produce clarification. Do not resolve by list index, nearest region or similarity guessed by the model. Unresolved objects remain available for source inspection and are excluded from mesh selection/tours.

An explicit modeled-window selection means all renderable, reliably associated saved window records in the requested scope, never every window in the real building or drawing. Report renderable/unresolved coverage without claiming extraction completeness. Native IFC source navigation uses the existing pinned record inspector; do not invent blueprint pages. Drawings use the original stored page/region exactly, including existing coarse-region limitations.

Malformed actions, absent targets, unsupported edits and stale persistent revisions fail before execution. A provider failure is a recoverable operational error, never source insufficiency or silent regex/fixture fallback. Compact chat buttons may emit typed deterministic actions without another model call. Keep existing upload/page/provider limits; one small intent call adds routing latency, not a second factual review.

## State and sequencing invariants

1. On every submit, synchronously pause the tour and capture an immutable snapshot before any await or queued timer can change focused ID. Cancel queued tour movement. Resolve “this window” against that snapshot. Preserve the captured source revision and stored evidence separately from current display state.
2. Apply asynchronous results only to their request/document epoch. A newer scene swap revalidates selection and tour IDs; removed/unresolved targets are explained and never replaced by another object. Stale refinements return 409 and request an explicit resubmission against the refreshed revision. Old source evidence can still open its pinned revision.
3. Keep navigation selection/highlighting separate from answer highlights and assumption display. Source navigation pauses the tour but preserves its IDs/index, camera and model revision. “Back to the model; next window” restores that tour and advances exactly once. Reaching the end reports completion rather than silently cycling.
4. Camera top-down preserves selection. Frame selection from actual world bounds with active floor offsets; close-ups use reliable geometry/host orientation where available. An ambiguous orientation uses a useful oblique fallback labeled as approximate; never claim an inferred exterior side or physical dimension. import math
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator


class StrictModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)


class AskRequest(StrictModel):
    document_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)
    question: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    revision_id: str | None = None
    request_id: str | None = None
    conversation_id: str | None = None
    reply_to: str | None = None
    clarification_response: str | None = None

    @field_validator("question", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def trim_question(cls, value):
        return value.strip() if isinstance(value, str) else value


class Evidence(StrictModel):
    source_id: str | None = None
    source_page: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)
    page: int = Field(ge=1)
    bbox: list[float] = Field(min_length=4, max_length=4)
    label: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    observation: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1000)

    @field_validator("bbox")
    @classmethod
    def valid_box(cls, box):
        left, top, right, bottom = box
        if not all(math.isfinite(v) and 0 <= v <= 1 for v in box):
            raise ValueError("Evidence coordinates must be finite and normalized")
        if left >= right or top >= bottom:
            raise ValueError("Evidence must have positive area")
        return box


class Proposal(StrictModel):
    text: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    basis: Literal["explicit_assumption", "reference"]
    reference: str | None = None


class Operand(StrictModel):
    value: float
    evidence_index: int = Field(ge=0)
    unit: str | None = None
